stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
stimulus: In the eighteenth century, silk weavers in London's Spitalfields district produced fabrics of remarkable complexity, using pattern-weaving techniques that refugee artisans had carried with them from France. Few of the designers' working materials survive. One pattern book from the period, now preserved in a museum archive, ______ more than two hundred hand-painted designs for brocaded silk, each annotated with notes on thread colors.
explanation: The subject of the sentence is "One pattern book," and it has no main verb yet. The phrase "now preserved in a museum archive" is only an interrupter. You need a finite verb, and "contains" is the only tensed form. It gives the sentence its main verb and agrees with the singular subject.

A.why: "Containing" sounds smooth, but an -ing form can't be the main verb of a clause. With it, "One pattern book" never gets a verb, and the sentence becomes a fragment.

B.why: "To contain" is an infinitive. It can't be a main verb, so the subject "One pattern book" is left without a predicate.

D.why: "Having contained" is a participle phrase, not a tensed verb. The sentence still has no main verb, and the perfect form clashes with a book that holds these designs now.

stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
stimulus: Before satellite imagery existed, mapmakers charted coastlines through a painstaking process called triangulation. On one nineteenth-century survey of a rocky northern shoreline, the field team first measured a single baseline across a flat stretch of beach with steel chains and ______ the angles from each end of that line to distant church towers and hilltops.
explanation: The word "and" joins two actions done by the same subject, "the field team." The first action is "measured," a simple past verb. The second action has to be parallel with it, so the answer is "recorded."

B.why: "Recording" is an -ing form. After "and," it doesn't match "measured," so the compound predicate is broken. You probably picked the form that sounded most fluent.

C.why: "To record" is an infinitive. It can't serve as the second verb in a compound predicate that begins with the past-tense verb "measured."

D.why: "Having recorded" is a participle, not a finite verb. It doesn't match "measured," and it suggests the recording happened before the measuring.

stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
stimulus: Light from the most distant galaxies has traveled for billions of years, and over that time the expansion of the universe has stretched it into infrared wavelengths invisible to the human eye. Shielded from the Sun's heat by a layered sunshade roughly the size of a tennis court, the orbiting telescope ______ that faint infrared glow with detectors cooled to just a few degrees above absolute zero.
explanation: The sentence opens with a modifier that ends in a comma, and the subject "the orbiting telescope" comes right after it. That subject still needs a main verb. "Detects" is the only finite choice, and it agrees with the singular subject.

A.why: "Detecting" can't serve as a main verb. The sentence would be a long description of the telescope with nothing for the telescope to actually do.

C.why: "To detect" is an infinitive. It isn't a tensed verb, so the subject "the orbiting telescope" is left without a predicate.

D.why: "Having detected" is a participle phrase. It gives the subject no main verb, so the sentence is a fragment.

stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
stimulus: Nutrition researchers have long debated whether dietary fiber meaningfully reduces appetite later in the day. In a trial led by nutrition scientist Priya Raman, adult volunteers were randomly assigned one of two breakfasts of equal calories. The participants who ate a high-fiber breakfast of oats, lentils, and berries ______ significantly fewer calories at lunch than those who ate a low-fiber breakfast.
explanation: The subject is "The participants." The clause "who ate a high-fiber breakfast of oats, lentils, and berries" already has its own verb, "ate," but the main subject still needs one. "Consumed" is finite and past tense, which matches the past-tense report of the trial.

A.why: "Consuming" isn't a finite verb. You may have taken "ate" as the sentence's main verb, but it belongs to the "who" clause. The main subject "The participants" still has no verb of its own.

B.why: "To consume" is an infinitive. It leaves "The participants" without a main verb, so the sentence is a fragment.

C.why: "Having consumed" is a participle phrase. It can't serve as the main verb, so the subject "The participants" is still waiting for one.

explanation: The subject is "a field," and "planted with cover crops" only describes it. The subject has no main verb yet. "Loses" is finite, agrees with the singular "field," and matches the present tense the passage uses for general facts.

A.why: "Losing" is an -ing form. It leaves "a field" without a main verb, so the sentence reads fluently but is a fragment.

B.why: "To lose" is an infinitive and can't be the main verb, so the subject "a field" still has no predicate.

D.why: "Having lost" is a participle phrase, not a tensed verb. The sentence still lacks a main verb.

stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
stimulus: Linguist Tomás Ferreira spent three years documenting a dialect spoken today in only a handful of mountain villages, where fewer than two hundred fluent speakers remain. Working with a small team of local volunteers, he interviewed elderly residents about their childhoods and ______ hundreds of hours of their conversations, marking the distinctive vowel sounds that set the dialect apart.
explanation: The word "and" joins two actions done by the same subject, "he." The first action is the past-tense verb "interviewed," so the second must be the parallel past-tense verb "transcribed."

A.why: "Transcribing" is an -ing form. It doesn't match "interviewed" after "and," so the compound predicate falls apart.

B.why: "To transcribe" is an infinitive. It can't be paired with the finite verb "interviewed" as a second action by the same subject.

C.why: "Having transcribed" is a participle, not a finite verb. It breaks the parallel with "interviewed" and wrongly suggests the transcribing came first.

explanation: Cross out the prepositional phrases ("of survey responses," "from more than four thousand warehouse employees"), and you're left with the subject "Her recent analysis" with no verb. "Suggests" is the only finite choice, and it agrees with the singular subject.

A.why: "Suggesting" is an -ing form. It sounds natural after "employees," but it leaves "Her recent analysis" without a main verb, so the sentence is a fragment.

C.why: "To suggest" is an infinitive and can't be the main verb, so the subject "Her recent analysis" has no predicate.
